note: Student-ready key facts for the Portrait Day design activity. Action lists include major achievements, consequential choices, and important controversies when needed for historical accuracy.

presidents.name: George Washington
presidents.education: No college degree; trained as a surveyor
keyAccomplishments: Created the presidential Cabinet, the president’s group of top advisers
Set the two-term example that later presidents followed
Kept the nation out of the European war in the European war
importantQuotes: I hope I shall always possess firmness and virtue enough to maintain the character of an Honest Man.
The proposed Constitution . . . is provided with more checks and barriers against the introduction of Tyranny . . . than any Government hitherto instituted among mortals.

presidents.name: John Adams
keyAccomplishments: Signed the controversial Alien and Sedition Acts
importantQuotes: Swim or sink, live or die, survive or perish with my country was my unalterable determination.
The institutions now made in America will not wholly wear out for thousands of years. It is of the last importance, then, that they should begin right.
People and nations are forged in the fires of adversity.

presidents.name: Thomas Jefferson
presidents.religion: No official church; influenced by Deism and Unitarian Christianity
keyAccomplishments: Sponsored the Lewis and Clark expedition
importantQuotes: I have sworn upon the altar of God eternal hostility against every form of tyranny over the mind of man.
The care of human life and happiness, and not their destructions, is the first and only legitimate object of good government.
A little rebellion now and then is a good thing, and as necessary in the political world as storms in the physical.

presidents.name: James Madison
presidents.education: College of New Jersey, now Princeton
keyAccomplishments: Led the country during the War of 1812
Supported rebuilding national money and banking system
Approved the Second Bank of the United States
importantQuotes: There never was an assembly of men who were more pure in their motives, or more . . . devoted to the object committed to them.
To have shrunk [from war], would have acknowledged . . . [that] the American people were not an independent people, but colonists and vassals.
Justice is the end of government. It ever has been, and ever will be pursued, until it be obtained, or until liberty be lost in the pursuit.

presidents.name: James Monroe
presidents.education: College of William and Mary; studied law under Jefferson
importantQuotes: The American continents . . . are henceforth not to be considered as subjects for future colonization by any European powers.
Yes, papa, but we haven’t any roads like this.
That’s true. Our country may be likened to a new house. We lack many things, but we possess the most precious of all – liberty!

presidents.name: John Quincy Adams
keyAccomplishments: Promoted roads, canals, science, and education
importantQuotes: Make no mistake about it, the four most miserable years of my life were my four years in the Presidency.
America does not go abroad in search of monsters to destroy.

presidents.name: Andrew Jackson
keyAccomplishments: Enforced the destructive Indian Removal policy
importantQuotes: The great can protect themselves, but the poor and humble require the arm and shield of the law.
Our Federal Union—it must be preserved.

presidents.name: Martin Van Buren
importantQuotes: I cannot expect to perform the task with equal ability and success.
As to the Presidency, the two happiest days of my life were those of my entrance upon the office and my surrender of it.

presidents.name: William Henry Harrison
presidents.education: Hampden-Sydney College and medical study at Pennsylvania; no degree
keyAccomplishments: His death tested rules for replacing a president
importantQuotes: The job seekers pack the White House every day. They pursue me so closely that I can not even attend to the necessary functions of nature.
The people are the only legitimate fountain of power.

presidents.name: John Tyler
keyAccomplishments: Established that the vice president fully becomes president
Supported adding Texas to the United States
Broke with his own Whig Party
importantQuotes: I can never consent to being dictated to.
The Constitution will be my guide.

presidents.name: James K. Polk
keyAccomplishments: Expanded U.S. territory after the Mexican-American War
importantQuotes: In truth, though I occupy a very high position, I am the hardest working man in this country.
I prefer to supervise the whole operations of the Government myself rather than entrust the public business to subordinates and this makes my duties very great.
No President who performs his duties faithfully and conscientiously can have any leisure.

presidents.name: Zachary Taylor
presidents.education: Limited formal schooling; career military training
keyAccomplishments: Opposed expanding slavery into western territories
importantQuotes: I have no private purpose to accomplish, no party objectives to build up, no enemies to punish.
Let us always be just, and in our magnanimity never forget to be vigilant.

presidents.name: Millard Fillmore
keyAccomplishments: Sent the expedition that opened relations with Japan
importantQuotes: The Constitution has made it the duty of the President to take care that the laws be faithfully executed.
An honorable defeat is better than a dishonorable victory.

presidents.name: Franklin Pierce
keyAccomplishments: Saw violent conflict between the North and South intensify
importantQuotes: I believe that involuntary servitude, as it exists in different States of this Confederacy, is recognized by the Constitution.
You have summoned me in my weakness; you must sustain me by your strength.

presidents.name: James Buchanan
keyAccomplishments: Failed to stop the crisis over states leaving the United States
Remained in office as seven states left the United States
importantQuotes: If you are as happy on entering the White House as I on leaving, you are a very happy man indeed.
The ballot box is the surest arbiter of disputes among free men.

presidents.name: Abraham Lincoln
presidents.education: About one year of formal schooling; self-educated in law
importantQuotes: Abraham Lincoln his hand and pen he will be good but god knows When.
House Divided
Somewhat like the boy in Kentucky who stubbed his toe while running to see his sweetheart. The boy said he was too big to cry, and far too badly hurt to laugh.

presidents.name: Andrew Johnson
importantQuotes: I voted against Lincoln. I spoke against him. I spent my money to defeat him. But still I love my country.
The goal to strive for is a poor government but a rich people.

presidents.name: Ulysses S. Grant
presidents.education: United States Military Academy at West Point
keyAccomplishments: Enforced civil rights during Reconstruction, the effort to rebuild after the Civil War
importantQuotes: No terms except an unconditional and immediate surrender can be accepted.
Mistakes have been made . . and I admit [them. But] failures have been errors of judgment, not of intent.

presidents.name: Rutherford B. Hayes
presidents.education: Kenyon College and Harvard Law School
keyAccomplishments: Promoted civil-service reform, or government hiring based on skill
Withdrew federal troops from the South
importantQuotes: He serves his party best who serves the country best.
The President of the United States of necessity owes his election to office to the suffrage and zealous labors of a political party.

presidents.name: James A. Garfield
keyAccomplishments: Challenged the patronage system of giving government jobs to political supporters
Defended federal education and civil rights
Was assassinated months after taking office
importantQuotes: My God, what is there in this place that a man should ever want to get in it?
We shall never know why slavery dies so hard in this Republic . . . till we know why Sin is long-lived and Satan is immortal.

presidents.name: Chester A. Arthur
keyAccomplishments: Signed the Pendleton Civil Service Act
importantQuotes: I may be President of the United States, but my private life is nobody’s damned business.
Men may die, but the fabrics of our free institutions remain unshaken.

presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
keyAccomplishments: Used the veto more than earlier presidents
importantQuotes: The truly American sentiment recognizes the dignity of labor and the fact that honor lies in natural toil.
He mocks the people who proposes that the government shall protect the rich and that they in turn will care for the laboring poor.
Federal aid in such cases encourages the expectation of paternal care on the part of the Government and weakens the sturdiness of our national character.

presidents.name: Benjamin Harrison
importantQuotes: We Americans have no commission from God to police the world.
The ballot is the only safety.

presidents.name: William McKinley
presidents.education: Allegheny College and Albany Law School; no degree
keyAccomplishments: Led the nation in the Spanish-American War
importantQuotes: I have never been in doubt since I was old enough to think intelligently that I would someday be made President.
That’s all a man can hope for during his lifetime––to set an example––and when he is dead, to be an inspiration to history.
Illiteracy must be banished from the land if we shall attain that high destiny as the foremost of the enlightened nations of the world which, under Providence, we ought to achieve.

presidents.name: Theodore Roosevelt
presidents.education: Harvard College; attended Columbia Law School
keyAccomplishments: Advanced construction of the Panama Canal
importantQuotes: Get action. Do things; be sane; don’t fritter away your time; create, act, take a place wherever you are and be somebody; get action.
The joy of living is his who has the heart to demand it. Life is a great adventure, and I want to say to you, accept it in such a spirit.
The first requisite of a good citizen in this Republic of ours is that he shall be able and willing to pull his weight.

presidents.name: William Howard Taft
presidents.education: Yale College and Cincinnati Law School
keyAccomplishments: Filed major antitrust, or anti-monopoly cases
importantQuotes: Our international policy is always to promote peace.
Machine politics and the spoils system are as much an enemy of a proper and efficient government system of civil service as the boll weevil is of the cotton crop.
Anti-semitism is a noxious weed that should be cut out. It has no place in America.

presidents.name: Woodrow Wilson
presidents.education: Princeton University and Johns Hopkins University; attended Virginia Law
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Lawyer, Professor, College Administrator, Public Official
keyAccomplishments: Created the Federal Reserve, the nation’s central banking system
Led the nation during World War I
Promoted the League of Nations while separating federal workers by race
importantQuotes: No one but the President seems to be expected . . . to look out for the general interests of the country.
The world must be made safe for democracy.

presidents.name: Warren G. Harding
keyAccomplishments: Supported treaties that limited weapons after World War I
His administration was damaged by major scandals
importantQuotes: In the great fulfillment we must have a citizenship less concerned about what the government can do for it and more anxious about what it can do for the nation.
We must stabilize and strive for normalcy.
I am just beginning to realize what a job I have taken over. God help me, for I need it.

presidents.name: Calvin Coolidge
importantQuotes: The business of America is business.
There is no dignity quite so impressive, and no independence quite so important, as living within your means.
It is the duty of a citizen not only to observe the law but to let it be known that he is opposed to its violation.

presidents.name: Herbert Hoover
keyAccomplishments: Expanded public works during the Depression
Failed to stop the economic collapse
importantQuotes: We in America today are nearer to the final triumph over poverty than ever before in the history of any land.
Every time the government is forced to act, we lose something in self-reliance, character and initiative.

presidents.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
presidents.education: Harvard College; attended Columbia Law School
keyAccomplishments: Created New Deal relief and reform programs
Led the nation through most of World War II
Ordered the incarceration of Japanese Americans
importantQuotes: The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
The only limit to our realization of tomorrow will be our doubts of today.

presidents.name: Harry S. Truman
presidents.education: High school; attended business and law courses without a degree
keyAccomplishments: Approved the Marshall Plan and NATO
importantQuotes: The menace of communism lies primarily in those areas of American life where the promise of democracy remains unfulfilled.
Every segment of our population, and every individual, has a right to expect from his government a fair deal.
It’s a recession when your neighbor loses his job. It’s a depression when you lose yours.

presidents.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
presidents.education: United States Military Academy at West Point
keyAccomplishments: Created the Interstate Highway System, the national network of major highways
Enforced school desegregation in Little Rock
Warned about the close relationship between the military, government, and defense companies
importantQuotes: Well, not at the time. But I was scared stiff three weeks later when I got around to reading the newspaper accounts.
military-industrial complex,
The middle of the road is all of the usable surface. The extremes, right and left, are in the gutters.

presidents.name: John F. Kennedy
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Writer, Navy Officer, Journalist, Public Official
keyAccomplishments: Committed the nation to a Moon landing
importantQuotes: New Frontier
All free men, wherever they may live, are citizens of Berlin, and, therefore, as a free man, I take pride in the words––Ich bin ein Berliner (I am a Berliner)!’

presidents.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
keyAccomplishments: Signed the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts
importantQuotes: This administration, today, here and now, declares unconditional war on poverty.
The women of America represent a reservoir of talent that is still underused. It is too often underpaid, and almost always underpromoted.

presidents.name: Richard Nixon
presidents.education: Whittier College and Duke Law School
importantQuotes: Let us begin by committing ourselves to the truth––to see it like it is, and tell it like it is––to find the truth, to speak the truth, and to live the truth.
The greatest honor history can bestow is the title of peacemaker.

presidents.name: Gerald Ford
presidents.education: University of Michigan and Yale Law School
importantQuotes: It can go on and on, or someone must write ‘The End’ to it. I have concluded that only I can do that. And if I can, I must.
I hope historians will write that the Ford administration healed the land, that I restored public confidence in the White House and in the government.

presidents.name: Jimmy Carter
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Farmer, Navy Officer, Public Official, Professor
keyAccomplishments: Made human rights central to foreign policy
importantQuotes: We must adjust to changing times and still hold to unchanging principles.
We are a purely idealistic nation, but let no one confuse our idealism with weakness.

presidents.name: Ronald Reagan
keyAccomplishments: Negotiated arms reductions with the Soviet Union
importantQuotes: to believe that together with God’s help we can and will resolve the problems which now confront us. And, after all, why shouldn’t we believe that? We are Americans.
Government is not the solution to our problem; government is the problem.

presidents.name: George H. W. Bush
keyAccomplishments: Led the coalition in the Gulf War
Signed the Americans with Disabilities Act
Managed the end of the Cold War
importantQuotes: Make no mistake, a new breeze is blowing across the steps and the cities of the Soviet Union. Why not, then, let this spirit of openness grow, let more barriers come down.
We can find meaning and reward by serving some purpose higher than ourselves.

presidents.name: Bill Clinton
presidents.education: Georgetown University, Oxford University, and Yale Law School
keyAccomplishments: Presided over economic growth and budget surpluses
Was impeached by the House but not removed by the Senate
importantQuotes: There is nothing wrong with America that cannot be cured by what is right with America.
Our democracy must be not only the envy of the world but the engine of our own renewal.

presidents.name: George W. Bush
presidents.education: Yale University and Harvard Business School
keyAccomplishments: Led the response to the September 11 attacks
Launched wars in Afghanistan and Iraq
importantQuotes: I kind of figure life is going to work its way out somehow.
Today, we affirm a new commitment to live out our nation’s promise through civility, courage, compassion and character.
We will pass through this time of peril and carry on the work of peace. We will defend our freedom. We will bring freedom to others, and we will prevail.

presidents.name: Barack Obama
presidents.education: Occidental College, Columbia University, and Harvard Law School
keyAccomplishments: Led recovery from the Great Recession
importantQuotes: Yes, we can.
We reject as false the choice between our safety and our ideals.

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.education: Fordham University and University of Pennsylvania
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Real Estate Businessman and Reality TV Personality
importantQuotes: We will make America great again.
The forgotten men and women of our country will be forgotten no longer.

presidents.name: Joe Biden
presidents.education: University of Delaware and Syracuse University College of Law
keyAccomplishments: Signed major infrastructure and climate legislation
Signed the CHIPS and Science Act
importantQuotes: This is America’s day. This is democracy’s day.
We must end this uncivil war that pits red against blue.
